transcript.content: Hello, I'm Dr. Smith. What brings you in today?

I don’t get any enjoyment out of the things I used to love doing, and I can’t make myself start anything anymore. I used to spend hours on my model railways and woodworking, but now I just sit there in my workshop staring at them without any spark.
How long have you been feeling this way, and have you had similar periods in the past?

It’s been going on for about a month now, starting right after a promising work contract fell through. I’ve never experienced a period like this before; this is the first time I've ever felt this way.
Do you still experience moments of feeling better or some relief in mood when engaging in activities you usually enjoy, or does the low mood stay constant throughout the day?

No, the feeling is pretty constant and there's no real relief. Even when I try to sit in front of my model railway or a half-built cabinet, there’s absolutely no spark or pleasure in it. It honestly feels like the enjoyment has been completely switched off in my brain.
Have you also noticed a change in your appetite or weight recently?

Yes, I’ve had almost no interest in food for the past few weeks. Often, I’ll realize at four in the afternoon that I’ve only had a cup of coffee and a piece of toast. I really only eat because I know I should, not because I actually feel hungry.
Have you been having trouble with your sleep, such as waking up too early and not being able to go back to sleep, or sleeping more than usual?

Yes, I've been having major trouble with my sleep. Most nights I lie awake until two or three in the morning with my mind looping through worries about work and money, and then I wake up multiple times and get up feeling like I never really slept.
Have you been feeling excessively guilty or blaming yourself for things, even if they weren't entirely your fault?

Yes, I keep telling myself that losing those consulting contracts was my fault and that I've let everyone down. I've even started feeling like a complete deadweight, and I catch myself thinking my sister and my ex would honestly be better off without me around.
Have these thoughts about being better off without you included any thoughts of harming yourself or ending your life?

Yes, to be honest. I regularly find myself thinking it wouldn't be so bad if I just didn't wake up in the morning, and on a couple of really bad days, I've actually pictured how I might end my life. I haven't done anything to act on those thoughts, but they are there.
